title: Children for the source tax tariff
purpose: For employees subject to source tax, ask whether they have children and go through one block per child. This decides whether each child counts (and whether it counts towards an H tariff), which gives the child digit and the H tariff.

stories.title: Ask each child's age status and household, only where the tariff needs it
stories.i_want: employees subject to source tax to say whether they have children and, for each child, whether the child is a minor or of age and in first education, and whether the child lives in their household
stories.so_that: Lonio can tell which children may count for the Zurich tariff code without asking anyone else about their children
stories.priority_reason: Lonio now computes the full tariff code itself instead of HR using the calculator (D-001). Without the children questions the child digit cannot be set.

acceptance_criteria.title: Children question only for employees subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee is filling in the onboarding questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio has decided whether the employee is subject to source tax (rule subject_to_source_tax)
acceptance_criteria.then: only employees subject to source tax are asked whether they have biological or adopted children, answered "yes" or "no", and the answer is required. Married employees and registered partners are asked about children of the employee or of either spouse or partner. Everybody else is not asked. The answer is recorded for source tax.

acceptance_criteria.title: One block per child, starting with the age status
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax answered "yes" to having children
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reaches the children questions
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee goes through one block of questions per child and can add another child or remove one. Every answer in a block is about that same child. Each block starts with whether the child is "Minor", "Of age and in first education" or "Neither", and this answer is required. An employee who answered "no" to having children gets no child block.

examples.name: Employee with children gets the age status question
Employee without children gets no child block

acceptance_criteria.title: 'Neither' ends the child's block and the child does not count
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax is answering a child block
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee says the child is neither a minor nor of age and in first education
acceptance_criteria.then: no further questions are asked about this child and the child does not count for the tariff code (child result 'Not counted'). If the employee changes an earlier child answer this way, answers to that child's questions that no longer apply are discarded on submission.

acceptance_criteria.title: Same household asked for every child who may count
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax said a child is a minor or of age and in first education
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee continues that child's block
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked whether the child lives in their household, answered "yes" or "no", and the answer is required. The answer decides which further questions follow for that child.

stories.title: Ask custody and common household for a minor child living with the employee
stories.i_want: employees subject to source tax whose minor child lives with them to say whether custody is shared or sole and, with shared custody, whether they live with the other parent and whether care alternates
stories.so_that: Lonio decides, as the calculator does, whether the child counts and, for non-married employees, whether it counts with H
stories.priority_reason: This decides the child digit and the H tariff in the tariff code that Lonio now computes instead of HR (D-001).

acceptance_criteria.title: Custody asked for a minor child in the household
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax has a child who is a minor and lives in their household
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee answers that child's block
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked about parental custody: "Shared custody" or "Sole custody". The answer is required and recorded for source tax. With sole custody no further questions are asked about this child.

examples.name: Minor in household - custody asked
Minor not in household - custody (shared/sole) not asked

acceptance_criteria.title: Common household and alternating care with shared custody
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax has a minor child in their household with shared custody
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee continues that child's block
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked whether they live in a common household with the child's other parent ("yes"/"no", required). Only if they do not are they asked whether the parents share care in alternation ("yes"/"no", required). Both answers are recorded for source tax.

acceptance_criteria.title: Child result for married employees and registered partners
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax who is married or in a registered partnership (both count as married for source tax) has a minor child in their household
acceptance_criteria.then: the child counts with sole custody, and with shared custody plus a common household with the other parent. With shared custody, no common household and no alternating care, the child does not count. (Alternating care cases depend on who contributes more to maintenance; see US-06.4.)

acceptance_criteria.title: Child result for non-married employees
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax who is single, divorced, separated or widowed (all count as not married for source tax) has a minor child in their household
acceptance_criteria.then: the child counts with H with sole custody, and with shared custody when there is no common household with the other parent and no alternating care. (Cases with a common household or alternating care depend on who contributes more to maintenance; see US-06.4.)

An employee who is single, divorced, separated or widowed is asked whether they have parental custody. Each employee gets only one of these two questions, answered "yes" or "no" and required. stories.title: Ask who contributes more to the child's maintenance
stories.i_want: employees subject to source tax to say whether they or the other parent make the larger financial contribution to a child's maintenance, where the calculator needs this
stories.so_that: Lonio decides whether a child in alternating care, or a child of a non-married employee living with both parents, counts for the tariff code and whether it counts with H
stories.priority_reason: This decides the child digit and the H tariff in the tariff code that Lonio now computes instead of HR (D-001).

acceptance_criteria.title: When the larger contributor is asked
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax is answering a child block
acceptance_criteria.when: the parents share care of the child in alternation, or the employee is not married for source tax (single, divorced, separated, widowed) and lives with the child and with the child's other parent
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked who makes the larger financial contribution to the child's maintenance: "Employee" or "Other parent". The answer is required and recorded for source tax. A married employee or registered partner who lives with the child and the other parent is not asked; the child block ends there.

acceptance_criteria.title: Result for non-married employees
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax who is single, divorced, separated or widowed was asked who contributes more to a child's maintenance
acceptance_criteria.then: the child counts with H if the employee makes the larger contribution and does not count if the other parent does. This applies to a minor child in the household with a common household with the other parent, a minor child in the household with alternating care, a minor child outside the household with parental custody and alternating care, and a child of age in first education living with the employee and the other parent. stories.title: Derive the child digit and the single-parent H tariff
stories.i_want: Lonio to derive the child digit of the tariff code and whether a non-married employee gets an H tariff from the results of all child blocks
stories.so_that: the computed tariff code matches the calculator without HR going through it
stories.priority_reason: The child digit and the H letter are part of every tariff code that Lonio now computes instead of HR (D-001).

acceptance_criteria.title: Child digit is the number of children who count
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee is subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio derives the tariff code from the latest answers
acceptance_criteria.then: the child digit is 0 if the employee has no children. Otherwise it is the number of children whose result is 'Counted' or 'Counted with H' (0 if none counts). For example, three counting children of a married employee with an employed spouse give C3Y, and one H child plus one non-counting child give H1N. Codes with more than 3 children have not been compared with the calculator and are checked before go-live (see OQ-calculator-coverage).

examples.name: No children
One child counted (married, sole custody)
One child counted with H
Only child does not count

acceptance_criteria.title: H tariff for non-married employees with an H child
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee is subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio derives the tariff letter from the latest answers
acceptance_criteria.then: an employee who is single, divorced, separated or widowed (not married for source tax) and has at least one child counted with H gets an H tariff. One H child is enough even if other children count without H (e.g. A1 + H1 gives H2N). A non-married employee without an H child gets no H tariff, even if a child counts. A married employee or registered partner never gets an H tariff.
